name: Blighter A422 air security radar
description: Ku-band FMCW e-scan radar, 180 deg per unit, elevation to 30 deg with W20S antennas, 20 km instrumented. Free-space detection 2.73 km at 0.01 m2 RCS, 4.87 km at 0.1 m2. UK-supplied to Ukraine in 2022.

detectRangeM.condition: 2730 m at 0.01 m2 RCS, free space, M10S antennas

elevationDeg.condition: elevation coverage — The published figure is an antenna elevation BEAMWIDTH, not a signed coverage sector. [0,30] is the ground-based reading of 'wide vertical elevation coverage up to 30 deg'.
elevationDeg.source: ATRI A400 series page; Joint Forces A422 report

rangeAccuracyM.note: Class median of the sourced surveillance radars: lib-r8ss 3; median 3 m.

azimuthAccuracyDeg.note: Class median of the sourced surveillance radars: lib-r8ss 0.8; median 0.8 deg.

elevationAccuracyDeg.note: Class median of the sourced surveillance radars: lib-r8ss 3; median 3 deg.

falseAlarmRatePerScan.note: Planning factor: PLACARD_PFA 1e-6 (src/model/types.ts) times about 1e6 range-azimuth-Doppler cells per scan of a 360° surveillance volume gives about one false alarm per scan over the whole coverage; this 180° radar is recorded at 1. No vendor publishes a false-alarm rate.

dwellTimeS.note: Planning factor: Blighter publishes no dwell or CPI. An electronically scanned radar sets its dwell in the beam schedule rather than by beamwidth over scan rate; the literature CPI of 20 ms for X/Ku-band drone-detection AESAs is used. Open literature on X/Ku-band drone-detection AESAs gives a CPI of about 20 ms at 5 kHz PRF (about 100 pulses; arXiv 2307.10326) and about 30 ms at 6 kHz (about 180 pulses; MDPI Drones 7(5):316), and notes that a 2.7 ms dwell barely resolves micro-Doppler. The A400 sheet (BSS-1311) gives a 1.0 s fastest 90° scan and a 0.25 s Drone Spotlighting scan but no dwell; for this FMCW e-scan the count is chirps per coherent processing interval.

pulsesPerDwell.note: Planning factor: Blighter publishes no PRF or pulse count. 20 ms dwell at the literature 5 kHz PRF gives 100 pulses coherently integrated. Open literature on X/Ku-band drone-detection AESAs gives a CPI of about 20 ms at 5 kHz PRF (about 100 pulses; arXiv 2307.10326) and about 30 ms at 6 kHz (about 180 pulses; MDPI Drones 7(5):316), and notes that a 2.7 ms dwell barely resolves micro-Doppler. The A400 sheet (BSS-1311) gives a 1.0 s fastest 90° scan and a 0.25 s Drone Spotlighting scan but no dwell; for this FMCW e-scan the count is chirps per coherent processing interval.
